Jurisdictional Highway System Plan are being used as guides for
the development of all transportation system improvements in Milwaukee
County and City of Milwaukee. These plans have considered General
Mitchell Field as an important land use concentration and major
air carrier airport and recommended the construction of the Airport
Spur freeway to provide an improved surface transportation facility
to serve the passenger, employment, and cargo activity demands
generated by it. These plans would have to be revised in order
to provide the same level of regional transportation service on
the arterial street and highway network that was originally provided
with the proposed construction of the Airport Spur. These revisions
would have to include additional reconstruction of the existing
arterial system to provide the required capacity needed to carry
the increased traffic loads.
This alternate was also deemed undesirable for the reasons the Airport Spur freeway was proposed earlier. The freeway proposal would accommodate the longer trips, and high speed demands of automobile, truck and modified rapid transit vehicles and remove this portion of through traffic demand from the adjacent surface arterial streets.
College Avenue is currently a 2 lane road between South 13th Street and Howell Avenue. The improvement of this road by Milwaukee County to a 4 lane facility similar to other county trunk highways is expected in the late 1970's.
